scenes.description: Open a lesson or section with a concise title and subtitle.
Close a section with compact retrieval points.

default: Apply it to a new example

scenes.description: Reveal and explain a physics equation step by step.
Draw an object, surface, force vectors, net force, and acceleration.
Plot labelled data and animate how a graph is read.
Animate transverse or longitudinal wave properties.
Build and animate a circuit from recognised components.
Animate solid, liquid, or gas particle arrangements and motion.
Visualise before-and-after motion in momentum collisions.
Visualise energy input, useful output, and waste flows.
Compare energy stores or transfers with animated bars.
Draw magnetic field patterns around magnets or conductors.
Build the atomic model with nucleus, electrons, and labels.
Animate alpha, beta, or gamma emission from a nucleus.
Demonstrate reflection, refraction, diffraction, or superposition.
Introduce a definition with symbols, units, and a focused visual hierarchy.
Compare two or more cases without repeating prose.
Show a traceable worked calculation with explicit reasoning steps.
Trace projectile motion with horizontal and vertical components.
Show tangential velocity and inward centripetal force.
Animate a spring-mass system, restoring force, and optional graph.
Resolve forces for an object on an inclined plane.
Show heating curves, temperature change, and energy transfer.
Navigate the electromagnetic spectrum, wavelengths, and uses.
Show harmonics, nodes, and antinodes on a standing wave.
Contrast electron drift, current, and resistance effects.
Connect field, current, and force directions in the motor effect.
Show induced current from changing magnetic flux.
Relate turns ratio, voltage, and changing core field.
Relate gas particle motion to temperature, volume, and pressure.
Show reactants, products, and energy in fission or fusion.
Draw principal rays for lenses, mirrors, or a prism.
Visualise orbital velocity and gravitational force vectors.
Trace the ordered stages of average or massive stars.
Compare alpha, beta, and gamma penetration through barriers.
